summary: Provision ephemeral 'partner-audit' Slack workspace + Confluence project with RBAC and channel lifecycle automation
description:
Issue summary: Security team is onboarding an external auditing partner and needs a timebound collaboration surface that includes a Slack workspace scoped to just the audit engagement, a Confluence project for evidence exchange, and automation to provision guest accounts, enforce RBAC, and auto-archive after the engagement window.

Background: Current partner/onboarding flows are manual and across multiple tickets. Security requests a gated, auditable pattern with templatized channels/pages, just-in-time guest invites, and a retention/auto-archive lifecycle so evidence does not remain indefinitely. This ticket requests a one-off provisioning flow and an automation template the platform team can reuse.

Impact: Without this, onboarding the auditor requires multiple manual steps from SRE, Security, and Platform which extends audit start date and increases risk of mis-scoped access. The auditor requires access by 2026-03-10 to keep the engagement on schedule.

Requirements: 1) Create a new Slack workspace or workspace-like channel namespace named 'partner-audit-2026' scoped to auditing vendor group. 2) Create a Confluence project 'Partner Audit - Q1 2026' with a pre-populated evidence page template and access controlled to the vendor group + security + PO. 3) RBAC: limited guest lifetime (30 days) with expiration and a self-revoke link; no ability to export channels or pages. 4) Automation: a provisioning workflow (Slack invite -> create Confluence space -> generate service account for webhook-> attach retention policy) triggered from a Jira transition or a short form. 5) Auditability: action log export for audit trail and notification to #security-audit on creation/close. 6) Post-engagement: automated archive of Slack channels and Confluence space with snapshot export to restricted S3 and removal of guest accounts.

Acceptance criteria: - Workspace/spaces provisioned and accessible by named vendor accounts. - A templated Confluence page exists with placeholders and share link. - Guest accounts have TTL and are automatically disabled at expiry. - Automation can be executed via an approved Jira transition and completes end-to-end in <15m. - Security confirms audit trail visibility.

Security considerations: Follow Third-Party Access Checklist (see links). Use tenant-scoped service accounts. All secrets stored in KMS. No external file attachments permitted in public channels.

Ops notes: Prefer using existing ephemeral-workspace automation runbook; if missing, create new reusable playbook.
comments: 2026-03-01 | Maya Chen: Opening ticket per Security request. Target start 2026-03-10. Please confirm assignee and ETA. Attached: vendor contact list in Slack DM.

2026-03-02 | Liam O'Connor: Assigning to Platform self-serve automation squad. First step: confirm whether we should create a new Slack workspace or use an ephemeral channel namespace in the company workspace. Security to clarify export restrictions.

2026-03-03 | Priya Verma (Security): Preference is to use ephemeral channel namespace within the company workspace to avoid cross-workspace federation. Must disable file downloads for guests and require MFA. Confirmed retention snapshot to secure S3 path 's3://redwood-audit-evidence/partner-audit-2026/'.

2026-03-04 | Liam O'Connor: Prototype automation flow created: GitHub PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-infra/pull/4567 includes Lambda to sequence Slack invites -> Confluence space create -> create Jira 'audit-engagement' issue link. Pending Security review for KMS usage and file restriction enforcement.
2026-03-05 | Maya Chen: Vendor has provided Google-managed accounts and confirmed they can accept guest invites. Please flag if any manual verification is required before the 2026-03-10 deadline.
